[ZackyD] GPT says the following;
The Tefal 9 Litre Flex Dual Easy Fry XXXL Air Fryer (EY9228) is PFOA-, lead-, and cadmium-free, but it does use PTFE (Polytetrafluoroethylene) for its non-stick coating.
Because PTFE is technically a polymer belonging to the broader chemical family known as PFAS, the distinction depends on how you define "PFAS-Free":
PFOA-Free: Tefal explicitly certifies that its coatings are completely free of PFOA (perfluorooctanoic acid), a harmful chemical historically used to manufacture non-stick products that has been phased out globally.
Contains PTFE: PTFE is a stable, inert fluoropolymer. Tefal and major health authorities maintain that solid PTFE is safe and non-toxic for cooking under normal temperatures. However, because it falls under the broad PFAS family umbrella, brands targeting strict "PFAS-free" status (usually meaning ceramic-coated alternatives) typically avoid PTFE entirely.
If you are specifically trying to avoid PFOA, this air fryer complies. If you are looking strictly for ceramic or completely fluoropolymer-free (non-PTFE) alternatives, this model does not fit that description.

At $141 and $144 respectively, both of these deals at The Good Guys offer excellent value, so the "better" purchase entirely depends on whether you prefer a drawer-style air fryer with dual zones or an oven-style air fryer with multiple racks.
Here is a side-by-side comparison to help you decide:

Why choose the Tefal Dual Easy Fry :
Meal Coordination: The standout feature is the removable divider. You can split the 9L space into a 5.5L and 3.5L zone, set them to different temperatures, and use the "Sync" function so both finish at the exact same time (e.g., chicken in one, chips in the other).
Easier Cleanup: Drawer-style air fryers are generally easier to wash in the sink than scrubbing wire mesh racks and wiping down the inside of a mini-oven.
Higher Discount: The Tefal model generally retails closer to the $250–$399 mark, making this $141 price point a steeper overall discount.
Why choose the Sunbeam FlexiFry :
Batch Cooking Flat Items: Because it comes with three racks, you can stack layers of food vertically. This is excellent for dehydrating, baking cookies, or cooking a large volume of flat items like wings or party pies without them crushing each other.
Visibility: It features an internal light and a glass door so you can watch your food brown without opening the drawer and letting the heat out.
The Verdict:
If you usually cook a "main and a side" simultaneously (like meat and veggies) and want easy cleanup, the Tefal is the better purchase. If you frequently cook large batches of snacks for a crowd, dehydrate foods, or want an internal light to monitor baking, the Sunbeam is the better option.
